posts.note: 2025 post reproducing a failed book pitch ('Don't Panic') written 'a year or two' earlier, with a short framing intro and outro. Logged: the two 2025 publication calls plus the pitch's market, event, access and reader-outcome claims. Not logged: about two dozen chapter-content descriptions ('This chapter will...', 'The book will include...') that describe intended contents of a book the author says was not sold, and advice or truisms ('Don't lie to your kids. They'll learn to see through it').

statements.quote: Now you, my dear readers, can imagine how great this book might have been, but live in the dreadful shadow world knowing it’s not going to be in your hands any time soon, unless you are personally in control of a publishing house.
statements.context: Opening of the 2025 post. The author reproduces a failed pitch for his book 'Don't Panic: How to Manage the Emotional States of You and Your Loved Ones' (two publisher 'bites' that were 'nibbles, not bids') and tells readers the book will not be published any time soon.
statements.note: Call about the author's own unpublished book. The escape clause 'unless you are personally in control of a publishing house' is a joke.

statements.quote: I’m sure I’ll get out another book soon.
statements.context: Closing lines of the post, after the full pitch text: 'That is the pitch. It's not a book. You can't buy it anywhere.' The author expects to publish another book soon.
statements.note: Author's own publishing plan; no title, publisher or date given.

statements.quote: Up until now, only therapists and scientists have had access to these awesome tools. This will change once people read this book.
statements.context: Pitch Overview section (pitch text written 'a year or two' before the post, per the author). Claim that the general public will gain access to mentalizing tools, so far used only by therapists and scientists, once the book 'Don't Panic' is read.
statements.note: Conditional on a book that, per the 2025 framing, was not sold and is 'not going to be in your hands any time soon'.

statements.quote: When you’re done with this book, you won’t be so worried.
statements.context: Pitch Overview section. Promised reader outcome of the book 'Don't Panic'; the author adds a disclaimer that this is not medical advice.
statements.horizon_text: When you’re done with this book
statements.note: Promotional efficacy claim from the pitch text; the book was not sold.

statements.quote: This is what I’ve spent years learning how to do, and it’s going to be a much quicker journey for you.
statements.context: Pitch Overview section. The author claims readers will learn mentalizing much faster than he did because he already made the mistakes.
statements.note: Promotional claim from the pitch text.

statements.quote: But you’re probably not gonna return it. Because people don’t do a very good job of that, but that’s a different problem.
statements.context: Pitch Overview section, right after the line that a reader who dislikes the premise 'spent $30 on the wrong book'. Prediction that readers will not return the book.
statements.note: Joke framing, but the underlying expectation (buyers rarely return books) reads as sincere. Implies a $30 price.

statements.quote: Just in the next few months he will be an invited speaker at: The 3rd Annual Key Opinion Leader Summit (Virtual), The American Telehealth Association (San Antonio), The 2nd Annual Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy Conference (Philadelphia), The American Psychiatric Association (San Francisco, twice), The International Conference on Emergency Medicine (Amsterdam), and The American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (New York, twice).
statements.context: Pitch Author Biography, written in the third person. List of upcoming invited talks at the time the pitch was written, which the author says was 'a year or two' before this 2025 post.
entities: Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy Conference
American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
statements.note: Event commitments from the pitch text. The 'next few months' horizon fell before the 2025 post date, so forward_looking is set false.

statements.quote: We foresee two large audiences for Don’t Panic.
statements.context: Pitch Target Audience section. Forecast of two audiences for the book: people suffering or worried about family members (about 20% of the US population at any given time) and buyers of self-help books (18.6M copies a year per the NPD Group).
statements.note: Market-sizing claim from the pitch text; the book was not sold.

statements.quote: This book has the potential to attain a global audience in subsequent translations, serving this same target audience worldwide.
statements.context: Pitch Target Audience section, about the first audience cohort (people worried about themselves or a family member). Claim the book could reach a global audience through translations.
statements.note: Hedged market claim from the pitch text; the book was not sold.

statements.quote: It’s also likely the most humorous book intended to help deep despair you are likely to have land on your desk, with, I imagine, limited direct competitors.
statements.context: Pitch section 'A Note About Patient Stories', addressed to the publisher. Estimate of the book's competitive position: the most humorous book on deep despair, with few direct competitors.
statements.note: Hedged competitive-position claim from the pitch text; 'I imagine' also hedges.

statements.quote: And even if they don’t, they’ll appreciate honest guidance about what to say when their own life gets heavy.
statements.context: Pitch section 'A Note About Patient Stories'. Prediction that readers who do not have to deal with another person's despair will still value the book's guidance.
statements.note: Borderline: promotional reader-reaction claim from the pitch text.

statements.quote: Mentalizing transformed my life, it has saved the lives of many, many scores of my patients, and it will transform the reader’s life.
statements.context: Pitch Chapter Outline, Chapter 1 'The Mentalizing Revolution'. Claimed outcome for readers of the book.
statements.note: Compound: past claims about the author and his patients plus a forward claim about readers. Promotional efficacy claim from the pitch text.

statements.quote: This communication mastery will transform your relationships.
statements.context: Pitch Chapter Outline, Chapter 4 'Empathy Superpowers: Mentalizing Others with Precision'. Claimed outcome for readers who learn the chapter's perspective-taking methods.
statements.note: Promotional efficacy claim from the pitch text.

statements.quote: Once you develop this secret sense, you’ll be able to resolve conflicts of all varieties.
statements.context: Pitch Chapter Outline, Chapter 6 'Resolve Conflicts like a Pro: The Mentalizing Secret'. Conditional claim: readers who learn to measure the emotional temperature in the room will resolve conflicts of all kinds.
statements.horizon_text: Once you develop this secret sense
statements.note: Conditional promotional claim from the pitch text.

statements.quote: It’ll remind you of the power of mentalizing and how, done well with persistence, it will totally transform your life.
statements.context: Pitch Chapter Outline, Chapter 11 'The Mentalizing Mindset: Embrace the Journey'. Claimed outcome for readers.
statements.note: Restates the Chapter 1 claim that mentalizing 'will transform the reader's life'.

statements.quote: If I do a really good job, you’ll learn how to build trust with yourself and others.
statements.context: Sample excerpt from Chapter One of the pitch. Conditional claim about the outcome for readers of the book's trust-building 'recipe'.
statements.note: Conditional promotional claim from the pitch's sample chapter.

statements.quote: When you Rewind, Rewind to when people were curious! It will save you from some very difficult conversations that go nowhere.
statements.context: Sample excerpt 'Distract and Return and Rewind'. Advice to use the Rewind technique only toward moments of curiosity, with a predicted effect for readers.
statements.note: Borderline: advice plus a predicted effect. Logged for the predictive reading.
